note.text:
An idiom is a group of words whose meaning is different from the meanings of the separate words. “He is behind bars” does not mean he is standing behind some bars: it means he is in prison.
• caught red-handed: caught while doing something wrong
• behind bars: in prison
• on the run: running away from the police
• take the law into your own hands: punish someone yourself instead of going to the police
• keep an eye on: watch carefully
• turn a blind eye: pretend not to see something wrong
• break the law: do something illegal
• cry wolf: give a false alarm
Learn idioms as whole expressions, and use them in the right situation.

worked_example.problem: What does “The thief was caught red-handed” mean?
steps: “Caught red-handed” is an idiom: we cannot read it word by word.
It means caught while doing something wrong.
worked_example.answer: The thief was caught while he was stealing.

pick.s: The police caught the thief ___ with the stolen phone in his hand.
e: “Behind bars” means in prison.
“On the run” means escaping.

pick.s: After the trial, the kidnapper spent ten years ___.
e: “Red-handed” is about being caught in the act.
He was in prison, not escaping.

pick.s: Please ___ my bag while I buy the tickets.
e: That means pretending not to see.
That means giving a false alarm.

pick.s: The prisoners escaped and are now ___.
e: That is about being caught.
They escaped from prison.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the idiom wrongly?

right.text: The boy cried wolf so often that nobody believed him.
Never take the law into your own hands.
The teacher turned a blind eye to the cheating, which was wrong.
The robber is still on the run.

wrong.text: The prisoner was happy to be red-handed at home.
wrong.explain: “Red-handed” means caught in the act of doing wrong.

wrong.text: We keep an eye on the thief to pretend we did not see him.
wrong.explain: “Keep an eye on” means watch carefully.

wrong.text: He broke the law by helping an old woman cross the road.
wrong.explain: Breaking the law means doing something illegal.
